datasets.title: Repeat photos of the dunes, 2007 and 2015 (HiRISE), and how far the sand moved
datasets.summary: Two HiRISE photos of the same 1.5 km of the Bagnold Dunes, eight years apart, on the same 1 m grid, and how far each 64 m square of sand moved between them.

grid.crs: IAU Mars 2000 sphere r=3396190 m, equirectangular (Esri wkid 104905)
IAU Mars 2000 sphere r=3396190 m, equirectangular (Esri wkid 104905)

limitations: One 1.5 km patch of the dune band, not every dune near the sites.
The sand surface itself is too smooth and changes shape too much to match square by square; only the edges of the sand are tracked, so the rate is an indication, not a survey.

Most sand edges barely moved: over all 137 usable squares the median shift is 0.96 m in 7.962 years (0.121 m per Earth year). The 40 squares (29%) that moved at least 1.5 px shifted a median 3.229 m (0.406 m per Earth year), like the published rate for these dunes (about 0.4 m per year, up to 1 m, towards the south-west). Taking only the squares that moved sets a floor of about 0.19 m per year on that number, so treat it as indicative.
Direction consistency 0.36 (1 = all the same way): the direction is not reliable. Shifts at the edge of the search box are left out as probably wrong (2 squares).
Different sun angles and haze in the two photos change shadows and the dark-sand outline a little.

uncertainty.basis: phase-correlation shifts are good to a few tenths of a pixel where the sand has texture
